newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Chrome output boosts Rustenburg.
newsitem.headline: Chrome output boosts Rustenburg.

text.p: Rustenburg Platinum Mines Holdings Ltd (Rusplats) can expect an additional seven million rand profit in the year to end June from chrome production at its Union section, officials said.

Union, which contributes about 20 percent of Rusplats' platinum output, began chrome production in 1992 and made a breakthrough last year when it sold 39,000 tonnes of metallurgical grade chrome in four spot deals.
Current production could reach 50,000 tonnes a year, Union chrome business unit project leader Piers du Plessis told analysts on a tour of Union operations.
"We will sell to anyone but currently all our customers are overseas," du Plessis said.
Du Plessis said since April 1996, the chrome business unit had repaid all development costs and still realised a reasonable profit.
"Expected net profits until end-June, 1997, should increase by about seven million rand," du Plessis said.
He said the unit had also secured a three-year frame contract of 60,000 to 80,000 tonnes per annum and negotiated two chemical grade spot market sales.
"We have a low cost resource, as mining overheads are covered by platinum and we have 60 years of proven ore reserves," he added.
